tactic: organiser sends slides and recording link with a folder expiry
subject: Your slides and the stage recording, Harborlight 2026
body:
Dear Iris,

Thank you again for 'Keeping a family office boring'. It was the session people kept quoting at the dinner, and the delegate scores bear that out (Fenwick will send those separately).

Your slides as presented, the stage recording and the photographs are in your speaker folder:
https://harborlightforum.org/speakers/2026/kestrelmoor

The folder stays open until 14 November. After that the files move to the archive and you'd need to ask me to reopen it. Please have a look at the recording before then and tell me if there's anything you'd want cut; we release it to delegates in the week of 23 November.

With thanks,
Tamsin

Tamsin Grell
Programme Director, Harborlight Forum

tactic: production team asks for a signed speaker release, form attached
subject: Recording release form needs your signature
body:
Hi Iris,

Ollie from the production team at Harborlight. The edit of your session is done: 38 minutes, we've taken out the mic drop-out at the start of the Q&A and the two minutes of room noise while the panel chairs were being moved.

Before we can release it to delegates we need the standard speaker release signed. It's attached (Harborlight_Speaker_Release_2026.pdf). Sign, scan and send it back to me, or if you'd rather the recording stays unlisted just say so and we'll leave it in your folder only.

Cheers
Ollie Pennard
Production, Harborlight Forum

tactic: organiser passes on delegate feedback, no link
subject: Delegate feedback on your session
body:
Dear Iris,

The delegate feedback for your session is in. 112 responses, average 4.7 out of 5, which puts you second across the two days.

I've pasted the comments below rather than make you log in to anything.

'Finally someone said the quiet part out loud: most of the value is in not doing things.'
'Would have liked more on the operational side. The boring framing undersold how much detail there was.'
'Best 40 minutes of the forum.'
'The three-line risk register slide is already on our office wall.'
'More time for questions please.'

Two delegates asked to be put in touch; I'll write separately about that.

Kind regards,
Fenwick Adair
Delegate Relations, Harborlight Forum

tactic: chair invites her back for 2027, new event site, decision deadline
subject: Harborlight 2027: would you come back?
body:
Dear Iris,

Harborlight 2027 will be on 5 and 6 October next year, same venue. The programme committee met last week and your name was first on the list for a return. We'd like to offer you either the opening keynote on day one or a ninety-minute workshop version of this year's talk, whichever you prefer.

The speaker information for next year is on the new site, https://harborlight2027.events/speakers, including the fee and travel arrangements, which are as this year.

We announce the first speakers in January, so I'd be grateful for a yes-in-principle by Friday 11 December. If the timing is wrong, tell me and we'll keep the door open for 2028.

Warm regards,
Hesper

Dr Hesper Vane
Chair, Harborlight Forum

tactic: organiser she met at the dinner says the slides email has been sent
body: Iris, it's Tamsin from Harborlight. Just sent the slides + recording link to your work address, shout if it's landed in junk. Lovely to meet you properly at the dinner. Still laughing about the dinghy and the harbourmaster.

tactic: finance team opens speaker expense claims with a month-end deadline
subject: Speaker expenses: claim form, deadline 31 October
body:
Dear Iris,

Speaker expenses for Harborlight 2026 are now open. We reimburse standard-class travel and one night's accommodation for all speakers.

Please submit your claim with receipts through the speaker expenses page:
https://harborlightforum.org/speakers/expenses

The deadline is 31 October, as our financial year closes that day. Claims received after that go into next year's accounts and are paid in February. Payment is by bank transfer to the account you give on the form, and this year's run goes out on 16 November.

Please don't send card or bank details by email; the form is the only place we take them.

Best wishes,
Priya Sandell
Finance, Harborlight Forum

tactic: organiser asks consent before passing her details to two delegates
subject: Two delegates asked to be introduced
body:
Dear Iris,

Two delegates have asked to be introduced to you after your session: a trustee of a family foundation in the north, and a private-client solicitor who said she's been trying to explain 'boring' to clients for a decade.

Our rule is that we don't pass on speakers' contact details without asking. Would you prefer we give them your firm's contact page (vennholt-partners.example/contact) or your intro booking link (book.vennholt-partners.example/iris/intro)? Or neither, which is also fine.

Kind regards,
Fenwick Adair
Delegate Relations, Harborlight Forum

tactic: host asks permission to point a listener at her notes page

tactic: host forwards a listener question and offers a follow-up segment
subject: A listener question I don't want to answer for you
body:
Iris,

A listener question I'd rather you answered than me. From a trustee of a small family trust, quoted with his permission:

'Ms Kestrelmoor talked about a one-page risk register. We have a 40-page one that nobody reads. How do you start cutting it down without the lawyers panicking?'

Would you be up for a ten-minute follow-up segment, or if that's too much, a written answer I could read out? Either is fine, and so is no.

Callum

tactic: podcast listener asks for paid advice on a family trust
subject: Heard you on Thornbeck Hour: a question about my mother's trust
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

I heard you on the Thornbeck Hour last week and found your notes site afterwards. I'm not in finance. My mother died in March and my sister and I are now trustees of a family trust of about £2 million, with an adviser who sends us 60 pages a quarter that neither of us understands.

Your point that a trust should have a one-page statement of what it's for and what it won't do made more sense than anything we've been told. Is this something you'd talk to two amateurs about for an hour, paid at whatever your rate is? If it's not the kind of thing you do, could you point us to who does?

Thank you for your time.

Hamish Drever

tactic: family-office head who heard the talk has booked an intro slot and introduces herself
subject: Introduction request, from Harborlight
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

I run the family office for the Fernshaw family and was in the room for your talk at Harborlight. I've booked thirty minutes through the intro link on your firm's site, Wednesday 4 November at 09:30; I hope that's the right route and not a liberty.

What I'd like to understand is how Vennholt structures its reporting to the family: frequency, length, what you leave out. We're rebuilding ours and I'd rather borrow than invent.

Kind regards,
Lucía Fernshaw
Fernshaw Family Office

tactic: student at her old school asks three dissertation questions
subject: Dunmorrow student: could I ask you three questions for my dissertation?
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

I'm a third-year undergraduate at Dunmorrow School of Economics writing my dissertation on governance in small family offices. My supervisor mentioned you studied at Dunmorrow and I watched your Harborlight talk on the forum's site.

Could I ask you three questions, either in a 20-minute call or in writing?

1. Is there a size below which a formal investment committee does more harm than good?
2. How do you stop the one-page risk register growing back?
3. What would you have told yourself in 2011, when you joined the firm?

My first draft is due 15 December, but I understand completely if you don't have time.

Yours sincerely,
Priyanka Rao

tactic: startup founder who saw the talk asks for feedback on his new site
subject: Would you look at what we're building? (saw your talk)
body:
Hi Iris,

I'm Tomas, founder of Tidewright. We're four months old and building reporting software for small family offices: one page, not sixty. I watched your Harborlight talk twice and winced both times because you described our product's reason to exist better than our website does.

https://tidewright.io

I'm not selling you anything; you don't need software. I'd like twenty minutes of your most brutal feedback on what's wrong with the idea. If that's a no, no hard feelings, and thank you for the talk.

Tomas Lindqvist

tactic: charity trustee asks who handles new mandates ahead of a formal RFP
subject: Introduction to our trustees?
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

I'm a trustee of the Aldwyn Trust, a charitable trust with an endowment of around £40 million. We will be reviewing our investment advisory arrangements in the first quarter of 2027 and I'd like to include Vennholt Partners in the process.

I found your profile on the firm's team page and, having heard your Harborlight talk, suspect your approach is what my fellow trustees have been looking for without being able to name it.

Could you tell me who at the firm handles new charitable mandates? A formal request for proposals will follow in January; this is only to make sure it reaches the right desk.

Yours sincerely,
Edmund Achterberg
Trustee, Aldwyn Trust

tactic: retired fund manager disagrees with a point from the podcast and notes
subject: Your notes on the boring portfolio: a disagreement
body:
Ms Kestrelmoor

I ran a balanced fund for 31 years and I think you're wrong about rebalancing bands, or at least about the 5% figure you gave on the podcast and in your notes. For a portfolio with illiquid holdings the band has to be wider or you end up selling the liquid book to fix a number that was never precise in the first place. We used 10% on the illiquid sleeve and never regretted it.

Otherwise I agreed with every word, which is why I bothered to write. Happy to be told I'm wrong.

Jonty Pelham

tactic: academic asks for an introduction to the forum organisers, paper attached
subject: Could you introduce me to the Harborlight organisers?
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

I'm a lecturer in organisational governance and I've just finished a paper on decision-making in small boards, attached, which I think sits alongside your Harborlight argument rather well. I'd very much like to present at Harborlight 2027 and I don't know anyone on the committee.

Would you be willing to introduce me to the organisers, or to tell me whether a cold approach to them is acceptable? I appreciate this is an imposition from a stranger.

With thanks,
Dr Anneliese Baur

tactic: listener writes to say thank you, no ask

tactic: new search boutique presents a managing partner role and asks for a short call
subject: New search firm, old-fashioned approach: a role you might dismiss
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

Rowe & Castellan is a new search firm; we opened in July, which you'll see from our website, https://rowe-castellan.site, and which I mention so you know what you're dealing with.

The role: Managing Partner of a multi-family office in the south-west with about £1.2 billion under advice. The current managing partner retires in 2027. The partners want someone who has run a firm of comparable size for a long time and who speaks publicly about doing it carefully. Having been managing partner at Vennholt Partners since 2011, you are an obvious name, which is why this will be the second or third such letter you've had this month.

I'd value fifteen minutes by phone, at a time you choose. If the answer is no, I'd still welcome your view on who else we should be speaking to.

Yours sincerely,
Dev Castellan
Rowe & Castellan

tactic: recruiter follows up with two meeting dates
subject: CIO search: the client would like to meet, two dates
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

Thank you for the call yesterday. The client would like to meet you informally, and has offered Wednesday 18 or Friday 20 November, either lunch in London or a morning at the office near Caldermere.

Could you let me know which you'd prefer? I'll confirm within the day.

Kind regards,
Georgina Pell
Pellbridge Search

tactic: recruiter presents an unpaid trustee role with an application link and deadline
subject: Trustee (unpaid): Caldermere Maritime Heritage Trust
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

Harrowgate Partners is helping the Caldermere Maritime Heritage Trust recruit two trustees. It's unpaid: four board meetings a year, one of them on the water, and whatever sub-committee work you volunteer for.

The trust needs someone who understands investment governance and who has a real connection to the Quay. Your membership of the Caldermere Trustees Association and your sailing are what put you on our list, together with the fact that you've spoken publicly about keeping things simple.

Details and the application form: https://harrowgate-partners.co/trustee-caldermere-maritime

Applications close Friday 4 December.

Kind regards,
Anwen Harrowgate
Harrowgate Partners

tactic: recruiter confirms shortlist and asks her to confirm an interview date
subject: NED role: shortlist and interview logistics
body:
Dear Ms Kestrelmoor,

I'm pleased to say the nominations committee has put you through to the shortlist for the NED role. The chair would like to meet you on Thursday 3 December at 10:00 in London; the address will follow once you confirm.

Could you confirm the date by reply? The committee will ask for two referees at the next stage; please don't send names yet.

Kind regards,
Harriet Fenmarsh
Fenmarsh Executive

tactic: recruiter she knows asks her to act as referee for a former colleague
subject: Not a role: a reference request
body:
Iris,

Not a role this time. Dara Whitlock, who was at Vennholt from 2014 to 2019 before moving to Hollins & Day, has given your name as a referee for a chief operating officer position I'm running. Would you be willing? If so, the client's chair would call you for ten minutes in the week of 9 November; tell me a time and a number and I'll set it up.

Marcus
